papers.title: Sub-nanofluidic Photochemical Membrane with Catalytically Active Channels for Solar Ammonia Synthesis
papers.abstract: Solar-driven conversion of N2 and H2O into ammonia under ambient conditions offers an alternative to the energy-intensive Haber–Bosch process, yet current advances are largely limited by material-focused strategies that insufficiently address coupled transport and interfacial reaction processes. Herein, we report a sub-nanofluidic photochemical membrane with catalytically active channels that integrate light harvesting, catalytic activation, and mass transport within a unified architecture for solar ammonia synthesis. The membrane consists of ZnIn2S4 atomically thin sheets and molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) quantum monolayers, forming ordered sub-nanometer channels that are intrinsically catalytic. This design establishes a confined reaction environment in which nanofluidic transport, gas–liquid interfacial regulation, and charge carrier dynamics are synergistically coupled. In particular, the combination of hydrophilic–hydrophobic interfaces and sub-nanofluidic-engineered serpentine flow pathways enhances reactant accessibility, residence time, and photon utilization, thereby overcoming diffusion and activation limitations typical of conventional photocatalytic systems. With these merits, the membrane achieves an ammonia production rate of 4.39 μg cm–2 h–1 (2.48 mmol gcat.–1 h–1) with ∼70% ammonia selectivity and maintains stable operation over 48 h of continuous testing. The achieved ammonia production rate compares favorably with those of reported photocatalytic platforms and some electrocatalytic N2 fixation systems. This work introduces a catalytically active nanofluidic channel paradigm for solar-driven N2 fixation and highlights the importance of material-transport co-engineering in bridging the gap between nanoscale catalytic design and device-level performance for chemical synthesis.

papers.title: Subnanometer Ni@Fe Catalysts Enable High-Performance and Stable Oxygen Evolution of WO3 Photoanodes
papers.abstract: NiFe-based catalysts are highly active for the oxygen evolution reaction, but their precise fabrication on photoanodes at subnanometer scale for accelerating charge transport and maximizing active sites remains a challenge. Herein, we report a facile approach to deposit trimesic acid (TA) coordinated subnanometer Ni@Fe hydroxides (Ni-TA-Fe) on nanoporous WO3 photoanodes. This WO3/Ni-TA-Fe photoanode exhibited a record photocurrent density of ∼2.4 mA cm–2 at 1.23 VRHE under AM 1.5 G irradiation (100 mW cm–2) with an enhanced stability, which is much higher than that of pristine WO3 photoanodes. Comparative experiments, characterizations, and density functional theory calculations revealed that the subnanometer Ni catalyst layers could effectively inhibit the dissolution of W atoms from the surface lattice and promote the structural stability of the WO3 photoanode during PEC water oxidation. Furthermore, the strong coordination and electron-trapping capability of TA could efficiently promote charge redistribution in Fe catalyst layers, resulting in the activation and transformation of surface Fe sites into high-valence Fe4+ species for significantly improving the OER activity. This work provides the viable pathway to active and durable bimetallic catalysts to achieve high-performance and stable PEC water splitting.

Photocatalytically Generated Nitrate Radicals Drive Decomposition of Perfluorooctanoic Acid
papers.abstract: Nitrate radicals (NO 3 •) generated in irradiated aqueous TiO 2 suspensions at acidic pH drive decomposition of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). The key role played by NO 3 • is demonstrated by the dependence of the reaction rate on the initial concentration of nitrate ions and by scavenging tests. The amount of nitrate ions remains constant during the process, indicating its catalytic behavior. The existence of nitrate radicals under the given conditions is here for the first time directly demonstrated by time‐resolved transient absorption spectroscopy. The process achieves ∼90% degradation of PFOA in 9 h with ca. 57% fluoride liberation. Theoretical results suggest that nitrate radicals trigger water‐mediated hydrogen atom transfer from the protonated PFOA, followed by decarboxylation and hydroxylation to the corresponding alcohol (experimentally detected), which eventually evolves to shorter‐chain intermediates. The proposed process represents the first proof of concept of the reactivity of NO 3 • with PFAS, but more importantly may be of practical relevance when coupled with the acidic regeneration of adsorbents currently used for remediation of water effluents containing PFAS.

papers.title: Unraveling the Importance of Surface Hydrogen Diffusion in Photocatalysis by Isotope Probing
papers.abstract: Harnessing solar energy for hydrogen generation has motivated extensive efforts to optimize photocatalysts, yet reported efficiencies remain inadequate due to insufficient mechanistic understanding. Using a well‐defined Pt/TiO 2 (110) photocatalyst, time‐resolved mass spectrometry, and isotope probing, we show that surface hydrogen diffusion can constitute a key, yet largely overlooked, determinant of photocatalytic hydrogen evolution. Employing selected methanol isotopologues, we disentangle the roles of hydrogen atoms from different precursor positions in the reaction mechanism. We find that replacing 1 H with 2 H (D) suppresses the hydrogen evolution rate, resulting from kinetic limitations by deuterium migration across the oxide surface. For CD 3 OH, we show that deuterium is removed from the surface via hydroxy‐H/D exchange, drastically decreasing the D 2 formation and bypassing the diffusion bottleneck. Our findings establish hydrogen mobility as a critical component of hydrogen evolution and highlight control of surface transport processes as a promising route toward maximizing photocatalytic performance in hydrogen‐involving reactions.

papers.title: Gradient Engineered Microporous Layers for Enhanced Oxygen Transport in PEM Water Electrolysis
papers.abstract: Microporous layers (MPLs) improve catalyst utilization in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), but must accommodate rapid oxygen removal at high current densities. Dense or poorly oriented MPLs can convert an interfacial benefit into a gas-transport penalty. Here, we introduce a gradient engineered MPL (G-MPL) where porosity and pore size increase from the catalyst side toward the porous transport layer (PTL). This architecture reduces voltage to 2.161 V at 5 A cm–2, outperforming uniform and reverse-gradient MPLs. Electrochemical analysis indicates the gain arises from reduced ohmic and transport-related losses, rather than from interfacial contact alone. Digital twin analyses show the pore gradient promotes oxygen evacuation and limits gas-filled regions restricting water access. Under limited water supply, the G-MPL retains stable operation at high current density. These results establish directional pore grading as an MPL design strategy for maintaining catalyst layer/PTL contact while managing oxygen-water transport in high current density PEMWE.

papers.title: Directing Hole Utilization Through Self‐Reconstructed Crystallinity Differentiation for Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation
papers.abstract: Photoelectrochemical water oxidation is limited not simply by light absorption, but by inefficient hole routing and utilization at the semiconductor‐electrolyte interface, together with severe defect‐mediated recombination. Here, a self‐reconstructed crystallinity‐differentiated interface is developed to program hole utilization in photoanodes. A one‐step hydrothermal synthesis creates an interlocked architecture in which highly crystalline In 2 S 3 pyramids are coupled with a disordered mixed‐anion nanosheet domain, generating a spatially polarized reaction field for directed hole accumulation and transfer. This reconstructed interface lowers the work function, redistributes the local coordination environment around In sites, and induces a spatially heterogeneous photovoltage landscape that promotes interfacial charge separation. Mild Ar annealing further serves as a defect‐selective activation step, suppressing recombination‐active defects while preserving the beneficial interfacial polarization, thereby accelerating charge injection and oxygen evolution kinetics. The optimized photoanode reaches 8.74 mA cm −2 at 1.23 V RHE , establishing interlocked crystallinity‐differentiated architecture engineering combined with defect‐selective activation as an effective strategy for sulfide photoanodes.

Constructing Electron Transfer Bridge between Organometal Halide Perovskites and Noble Metal Cocatalyst for Enhanced Photocatalytic Hydrogen Production
papers.abstract: Organometal halide perovskites (OMHPs) are attractive candidates for the photocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet the poor contact between OMHPs and the HER cocatalysts, like benchmark noble metals, seriously restricts the interfacial charge transfer and therefore the photocatalytic activity. Herein, by using two-dimensional (2D) OMHP phenylmethylammonium lead iodide (PMA2PbI4) as an example, we present an “electron transfer bridge” design to address this issue. In this design, metal sulfides, like nickel sulfide (NiSx), were preassembled on the surface of PMA2PbI4 via a facile adsorption approach. Benefiting from the strong chemical interaction between PMA2PbI4 and NiSx and the favorable electron-extraction ability of NiSx, the photogenerated electrons can efficiently transfer from OMHPs to NiSx. The electron-rich NiSx particles can then behave as the active sites for the following photodeposited Pt cocatalyst, which allows the efficient consumption of the photogenerated electrons to produce H2. Therefore, the sandwich-like architecture of the Pt-NiSx/S-PMA2PbI4 can leverage the high electron-extraction capability of NiSx and the efficient HER catalytic activity of Pt simultaneously, liberating the potential of PMA2PbI4 for photocatalytic HER. A photocatalytic HER activity of 693.2 μmol·h–1 was achieved with the optimum Pt-NiSx/S-PMA2PbI4, which is ca. 39 times that of PMA2PbI4. An apparent quantum efficiency of 25.1% at 450 nm was obtained, representing one of the highest values reported for 2D OMHPs.

papers.title: Solar-Driven Ammonia Production via Acidic Nitrate Reduction Coupled with Glucose Oxidation on a GeSe Photocathode
papers.abstract: Photoelectrochemical nitrate reduction (PEC NO3RR) enables nitrate remediation and ammonia synthesis under light irradiation. However, most reported systems operate under neutral or alkaline conditions to suppress the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), which compromises product separation and overall energy efficiency. Although acidic NO3RR is intrinsically favorable for stabilizing the ammonia product in the nonvolatile NH4+ form and suppressing ammonia loss, it remains fundamentally challenged by severe proton competition and HER dominance. Here, acidic NO3RR is intentionally established as a stringent design target rather than merely an operational condition. An electronically reconstructed CuNi cocatalyst is electrodeposited onto a TiO2-protected GeSe photocathode to steer the reaction selectively toward NO3RR under acidic conditions (10 mM H2SO4, pH ≈ 1.8). Ni-induced electronic modulation of Cu active sites positively shifts the onset potential, suppresses HER, and enhances nitrate-to-ammonia selectivity, achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 82.07% and an ammonia production rate of 14.32 μmol h–1 cm–2 at –0.1 V vs. RHE. To translate this selectivity to the system level, a solar-driven tandem PEC device couples the acidic NO3RR photocathode with an alkaline glucose oxidation anode via a bipolar membrane, enabling solar-driven ammonia synthesis.

papers.title: Electronic Modulation-Driven Dual Self-Reconstruction of a Nickel–Molybdenum Oxide Catalyst for Durable and Highly Efficient Anion-Exchange-Membrane Water Electrolysis
papers.abstract: Surface reconstruction of precatalysts during water splitting governs the formation of active catalysts, yet engineering robust dual-functional precatalysts that self-reconstruct into stable, distinct active phases under different hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) conditions remains challenging. Here, we tailor the in situ reconstruction of a self-supported nickel–molybdenum oxide precatalyst through the incorporation of iron and vanadium to control the formation of HER- and OER-stable active phases for efficient anion-exchange-membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE). In 1.0 M KOH, the as-prepared NiFeVMo requires overpotentials of only 25 and 207 mV to reach 10 mA cm–2 for HER and OER, respectively, while demonstrating stable operation throughout the durability tests conducted for approximately 302 and 192 h at 100 mA cm–2 for HER and OER, respectively. In an AEM water electrolyzer operating at 80 °C, dual-functional NiFeVMo used as both an anode and cathode achieves a current density of 1.0 and 4.0 A cm–2 at uncorrected cell voltages of 1.649 and 1.967 V, respectively. Combined experimental characterization and density functional theory calculations reveal cooperative electronic and structural effects arising from this multimetal material that lower reaction energetics, improve charge transfer, and stabilize the activated catalyst. This work provides a strategy for designing a PGM-free self-reconstructing precatalyst with dual catalytic activity, offering a promising approach for the development of earth-abundant and highly efficient catalysts for electrochemical energy conversion and storage technologies.

papers.title: Predicted, Rarely Validated: A Reality Check on Computational Electrocatalyst Discovery
Acidity-Driven Spontaneous Degradation of Trifluoroacetic Acid at Droplet Air–Water Interfaces
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), an ultrashort-chain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance, is increasingly detected in the environment and has raised widespread concern because of its negative effects on health and ecosystems. However, whether TFA can degrade naturally in the environment remains unresolved. Here, we report the spontaneous degradation of TFA at the air–water interface of droplets, yielding F– and fluorine-containing transformation products, including CHF3O, CF3O2H, and CH2F2O2. The extent of degradation is strongly dependent on droplet acidity, with the F– yield at pH 10 being 12-fold higher than at pH 5. Density functional theory calculations reveal a mechanism favored by alkaline conditions and oxygen in which interfacial decarboxylation triggers sequential oxidation and defluorination. These findings identify the air–water interface of pH-regulated droplets as a reactive microenvironment for spontaneous TFA degradation, offering new insights into the environmental transformation of ultrashort-chain PFAS.

papers.title: Microscopic Origins of Metal‐Dependent pH Effects in Hydrogen Evolution: Metal–Water Interactions Dictate Proton Transfer Pathways
papers.abstract: The hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is a prototypical proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) reaction, yet the atomistic origin of its metal‐dependent pH effect remains unclear. Here, combining constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics with in situ infrared spectroscopy, we unravel the microscopic origins of metal‐dependent pH effects in HER catalysis on Pt(111) and Au(111). We reveal that HER kinetics are governed by two competing spatial proton transfer topologies associated with the Volmer water‐dissociation step: a low‐barrier cross‐layer proton transfer (CLPT) pathway and a high‐barrier intra‐layer proton transfer (ILPT) pathway. For Pt(111), strong metal–water interactions yield a pH‐responsive water network. Under acidic conditions, a balanced intra‐ and cross‐layer hydrogen‐bond network promotes the CLPT in the Volmer step, thereby accelerating HER kinetics. By contrast, alkaline media induce a rigid H‐down interfacial water layer that favors the sluggish ILPT pathway. Conversely, weak metal–water interactions on Au(111) maintain a pH‐insensitive, predominantly parallel‐flat water orientation that restricts the Volmer step to cooperate only with the high‐barrier ILPT in both acidic and alkaline solutions. Our findings establish a fundamental causal link among metal–water interactions, interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network, proton transfer pathways, and HER kinetics, providing atomistic insight into the design of pH‐robust electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Suppressing Ru Deactivation Through Lattice Hydrogen and Hydroxyl Adsorption Engineering for High‐Performing Alkaline Fuel Cells
papers.abstract: Ru‐based catalysts demonstrate attractive activity and cost advantages for alkaline hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR), yet their practical deployment is limited by rapid deactivation at high anodic potentials in fuel cells. Here we identify reversible hydroxyl‐related surface passivation, particularly excessive *OH accumulation, as a key contributor to high‐potential Ru deactivation, and demonstrate that it can be mitigated through coupled regulation of *OH coverage and interfacial hydrogen supply. Guided by this mechanistic insight, we design a Pd‐core, tetra‐element‐ensemble Ru skin catalyst (Pd@Tees Ru), where electronic modulation of the multimetallic Ru shell suppresses excessive *OH accumulation, while the Pd core serves as a dynamic lattice‐hydrogen reservoir. Electrochemical evidence reveals the anodic release of interstitial hydrogen from the Pd core, sustaining *H coverage at the active interface and mitigating excessive accumulation of hydroxyl‐related surface species. Such synergistic interfacial regulation enables sustained HOR activity at potentials above 0.5 V. An anion‐exchange membrane fuel cell with the Pd@Tees Ru anode achieves a peak power density of 1.78 W cm −2 under H 2 /O 2 conditions and operates stably for 200 h at 500 mA cm −2 . By integrating lattice‐hydrogen dynamics with surface adsorption thermodynamics, this work provides a general strategy for mitigating passivation and improving the durability of Ru‐based electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Spin Polarized Chiral Co 3 O 4 Boosts High‐Pressure CO 2 Electroreduction to Ethanol With 90% Selectivity
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction (CO 2 RR) to value‐added multicarbon products using non‐copper‐based catalysts remains a major challenge, especially for selective ethanol production. Herein, we report that chiral Co 3 O 4 featuring strong electron spin polarization achieves a maximum ethanol Faradaic efficiency of 90% at ‐0.9 V versus NHE in KHCO 3 electrolytes under a 30 bar CO 2 pressure, substantially outperforming both racemic Co 3 O 4 and previously reported non‐copper‐based catalysts. The enhanced spin polarization in chiral Co 3 O 4 facilitates electron transfer and promotes the activation of the adsorbed CO 2 , while also lowering the free energy change for C–C coupling to form *COCHO intermediate, thereby promoting ethanol production. Our work establishes spin polarization as a key determinant for efficient C–C coupling on non‐copper‐based catalysts and provides mechanistic principles for the rational design of CO 2 RR electrocatalyst.

papers.title: Interweaving Two‐Dimensional Co‐Corrole‐Based Covalent Organic Framework for Significantly Improved Electrocatalytic Oxygen Reduction Reaction
papers.abstract: Two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising electrocatalysts but suffer from limited active‐site accessibility, sluggish mass transportation in narrow‐spaced interlayers, and interlayer sliding during catalysis. Herein, we report the synthesis of Co‐corrole‐based 2D COF 1 and its interlayer‐interweaved derivatives 2 and 3 for electrocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The reaction of Co tris(4‐formylphenyl)corrole and 1,4‐phenylenediamine gave 2D COF 1 with an interlayer spacing of 4.2 Å. Using pyrazine and bipyridine as bidentate molecular pillars to interweave 2D layers of 1 via bridging interlayer Co corroles, we obtained COFs 2 and 3 with interlayer spacing of 6.4 and 10.3 Å, respectively. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirmed that the expanded interlayer spacing is caused by the axial Co–N coordination between Co corroles and bidentate molecular pillars. Compared to 1 , COFs 2 and 3 exhibited markedly enhanced 4H + /4e – ORR activity and durability, with half‐wave potential increased from 0.80 to 0.89 V and 0.94 V versus RHE. Rotation‐rate‐dependent Tafel measurements revealed improved mass transportation in the enlarged interlayer spaces in 2 and 3 . The Zn‐air battery using COF 3 delivered a high open‐circuit voltage of 1.52 V and a large peak power density of 193.5 Mw cm −2 , outperforming Pt/Ru benchmarks.

papers.title: Bismuth–Sulfur Engineered Zero‐Valent Iron Prioritizes Chloramphenicol‐Class Antibiotics Dechlorination Over Hydrogen Evolution and Nitro Reduction
papers.abstract: Chloramphenicol (CAP) and florfenicol (FF), as chloramphenicol‐class antibiotics, often coexist in wastewater, where chlorine substituents largely determine their toxicity. Although zero‐valent iron (ZVI) is a promising reductive remediation material, its poor chemoselectivity and preferential electron consumption by hydrogen evolution (HER) and nitro‐reduction severely limit the detoxification of chlorinated moieties. Herein, we develop bismuth–sulfur co‐intercalated ZVI (Bi‐S‐ZVI) to reduce CAP+FF co‐contaminants, achieving enhanced nitro‐reduction (22–74‐fold), dechlorination (175–419‐fold), and low HER. Notably, the dechlorination selectivity (defined as the ratio of FF dechlorination to CAP nitro‐reduction) increased from 0.3%–2% to 39%, and Bi‐S‐ZVI enabled a distinct pathway where dechlorination preceded nitro‐reduction in the ‐NO 2 /‐Cl co‐substituted CAP molecule. Mechanistically, Bi 2 S 3 and Bi 0 are the dominant contributors to the reactivity and dechlorination selectivity of Bi‐S‐ZVI, respectively. Bi 2 S 3 couples galvanically with Fe 0 to generate a built‐in electric field and creates Fe–S–Bi charge‐transfer channels to accelerate electron transport. Bi 0 selectively associates with ─Cl as a halogen‐bond acceptor. Bi 2 S 3 and Bi 0 synergistically suppress HER by increasing surface hydrophobicity and hindering atomic hydrogen recombination, while Bi 2 S 3 further disrupts the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network. This work provides a cost‐effective and scalable strategy for selective reductive remediation, overcoming the reactivity–selectivity–stability trade‐offs of existing iron materials.

papers.title: Redefining Decoupled Water Electrolysis as an Integrated Hydrogen‐Carrier Platform
papers.abstract: The hydrogen economy is commonly organized around four separate tasks: production, storage, transport, and release. This Perspective redefines decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) as a framework in which these functions can be integrated within a single electrochemical redox loop. By using a proton‐coupled redox mediator to decouple hydrogen and oxygen evolution in time and space, DWE stores hydrogen equivalents in a charged mediator phase and releases H 2 electrochemically or catalytically at the point of use. This architecture shifts part of hydrogen logistics from pressure‐ or temperature‐intensive processes toward ambient‐condition electrochemical operation. DWE can therefore be viewed not merely as an alternative electrolyzer architecture, but as an integrated hydrogen‐carrier platform. Within this broader framework, this Perspective focuses primarily on solution‐phase proton‐coupled mediators because their charged inventories can function as transportable liquid‐phase carriers. Although current solution‐phase DWE mediators remain disadvantaged in gravimetric capacity relative to ammonia and liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs), their system‐level value lies in ambient‐condition storage, low‐temperature on‐site H 2 release, independent scaling of power (electrolyzer stack) and energy capacity (mediator inventory), and flexible coupling to intermittent renewable electricity. We therefore propose carrier‐relevant benchmarks including full‐system capacity, storage‐and‐release efficiency, mediator retention, gas quality, delivered cost, and closed‐loop logistics.

papers.title: In Situ Reconstruction-Directed Electrocatalyst Design Enables Low-Energy Anodic Oxidation for Water Purification
papers.abstract: Anodic oxidation reactions (AORs) hold promise for degrading persistent organic pollutants, yet practical deployment is constrained by inadequate anode stability and sluggish kinetics under low-bias operation. Prussian blue analogues (PBAs) feature cyanide-bridged metal frameworks with efficient intermetallic electron transfer, yet their surfaces inevitably undergo uncontrolled reconstruction during electrolysis, producing outcomes that range from beneficial activation to detrimental degradation. Here, we reported a first-ever paradigm shift from suppressing reconstruction to actively directing it, demonstrating that the intrinsic instability of FeMn PBA could be harnessed as a design lever. Through an in situ self-reconstruction process, we discovered that the morphology and surface coordination environment were spontaneously reorganized into FeMn nanoflowers grown on carbon paper (FeMn@CP), a configuration never before achieved from this precursor. This reconstruction-guided pathway uniquely yielded a 201-fold increase in electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) over pristine FeMn PBA, alongside markedly enhanced electrochemical stability, synergistic gains not attainable by conventional stabilization strategies. Capitalizing on this reconstructed architecture, FeMn@CP achieved efficient phenolic pollutant degradation at low bias, with robust reusability, broad matrix adaptability, and substantially reduced effluent toxicity. Continuous-flow experiments further verified its sustained performance under practical conditions. This study unveils, for the first time, that catalyst reconstruction, when rationally exploited, serves as a decisive and generalizable strategy to concurrently boost AOR activity and stability, opening an unexplored avenue for designing next-generation electrocatalytic water purification systems.

papers.title: Acetate-Enabled Selective Electrochemical Deuterolysis of Propargylic Carbonates
papers.abstract: Deuterated compounds are becoming more important in drug discovery, mechanistic studies, and materials science, yet their selective syntheses remain challenging. Here we report a powerful nickel-electrocatalyzed deuteration platform that converts readily available propargylic carbonates into deuterated allenes using D2O as a cost-effective deuterium source with a very high selectivity. The reaction delivers a broad range of deuterated allenes, including 1,3-dialkyl variants, which are very common in natural allenes, with an excellent level of isotopic incorporation. We have also demonstrated the synthesis of a deuterated natural product analogue and programmable access to mono- and dideuterated allenes with deuterium installed at one defined position or two. Mechanistically, electroreduction generates the active Ni(0) catalyst that initiates the catalytic cycle, whereas the acetate anion promotes efficient deuterolysis.

papers.title: Restructuring of Cobalt Telluride Electrocatalysts in the Oxygen Evolution Reaction
papers.abstract: Among non-noble metals, transition metal chalcogenide electrocatalysts have high electrocatalytic performance and electrical conductivity, but they experience restructuring in oxidative oxygen evolution reaction (OER) conditions. Unfortunately, it is unknown what triggers such restructuring. In this study, we used cobalt telluride (CoTe) as a model system and combined in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy with ex situ characterizations and DFT calculations to understand the restructuring mechanism. Results suggest that restructuring starts when CoTe is immersed in KOH solution and involves the transformation of Co–Te into Co–O bonds, suggesting that the true OER-active phases derived from CoTe are cobalt oxides or (oxy)hydroxides. The combined data are consistent with restructuring involving Te loss and oxygen incorporation at under-coordinated sites. Leached Te is detected in the electrolyte, while residual oxidized Te-containing species remain associated with the catalyst after restructuring. These observations are consistent with partial Te redeposition and/or retention of Te-containing surface species, which could influence the overall activity. Model-based analysis of the in-situ extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectra and XANES linear combination fitting suggests that the dominant reconstructed phases are Co3O4-like and CoOOH-like species that contribute to OER activity.

papers.title: Entropy–Enthalpy Compensation in Electrocatalytic Rates
papers.abstract: Measuring the temperature dependence of electrocatalytic reaction rates is a powerful, yet underexplored, way of investigating the underlying kinetics. In this study, we develop the understanding behind such kinetic measurements. Through a very simple model of the surface kinetics for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), we explore how extracted Arrhenius parameters depend on potential and rationalize a series of entropy-enthalpy correlations in experimental HER rates. We find that the entropy-dependent prefactor can change alongside the apparent activation energy, thus signaling deviations from the established Butler-Volmer kinetics that have so far mostly been attributed to potential-driven solvent dynamics. Distinct kinetic fingerprints emerge for different groups of metal catalysts that are in qualitative agreement with recent experiments. We elucidate these characteristic fingerprints in terms of shifting kinetic regimes and generalize our findings to other electrocatalytic reactions and setups. Our analysis overall suggests the entropy loss/gain due to species’ adsorption/desorption as the main driver behind measured changes in the Arrhenius prefactor.

papers.title: Operando Surface Dynamics Govern the pH-Universal Activity and Stability of Cobalt Phosphide for Hydrogen Evolution
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Cobalt phosphide (CoP) has been established as a highly promising, pH-universal electrocatalyst for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, the operando surface structure–activity relationship and the mechanistic origins of its high stability remain elusive. Here, we combine large-scale data mining (2,282 experimental observations), surface Pourbaix diagrams, ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), and microkinetic modeling to reveal the operando surface configurations of CoP. We demonstrate that at low overpotentials (<100 mV), the surface is dominated by HO*-covered configurations featuring P–OH groups. This P–OH enrichment critically modulates the electronic structure of adjacent Co active sites, optimizing H* adsorption and facilitating water activation. At high overpotentials (>100 mV), the surface undergoes a structural transition to a dense H* coverage (comprising Co–H and P–H species), which maintains highly favorable adsorption thermodynamics of H* near the Sabatier optimum (ΔGH* = 0 eV) across the wide pH range of 0–14 under the applied electric field. Surface coverage mapping and 2D microkinetic volcano analyses, using ΔGHO* and ΔGH* as key descriptors, further corroborate these potential-dependent surface species and the resulting high HER activity. Crucially, these potential-dependent surface adsorbates protect CoP from detrimental element leaching. Moreover, comprehensive experimental characterizations validate our theoretical predictions. This work exemplifies the capabilities of combining AI-driven data platforms with precise simulations in accelerating scientific discoveries and uncovering underlying catalytic mechanisms.

papers.title: Programming MOF Topology through Twelve-Connected Linker Isomerism
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Linker isomerism represents a powerful, yet unexploited, strategy for programming framework topology and unlocking chemical complexity in high-connectivity reticular systems. Here, we demonstrate the reticular synthesis of two 12-connected nanographene-based zirconium metal–organic frameworks, MOF-1300 and MOF-1400, wherein network architecture is directed by the meta versus para carboxylate substitution patterns of a 12-connected linker, dodeca-carboxylate hexakis[3,5-bis(m/p-carboxyphenyl)-4,6-dimethoxyphenyl]hexabenzocoronene (m/p-HBC-LH12). The meta isomer directs the assembly of an 8-connected cubic Zr cluster to yield MOF-1300 with an unprecedented trinodal (3,6,8)-c rcb1 net, representing a new topology in reticular chemistry. Conversely, the para isomer enforces 12-connectivity at the Zr cluster with hexagonal prismatic geometry to yield MOF-1400 with a rare trinodal (3,6,12)-c kex net which has not previously been observed in Zr-MOFs. Beyond structure, both frameworks serve as solid reservoirs of photoactive nanographenes: under basic photoredox conditions, they release their molecular HBC linkers, which act as homogeneous organophotoredox catalysts for the hydrodefluorination of polyfluoroarenes under simulated solar light (AM 1.5G). This behavior highlights the potential of reticular materials as precatalysts for the delivery of molecular photocatalysts and provides a basis for exploring such materials in future photocatalytic applications.

papers.title: Interfacially Stitched Bilayer Anodes Enforce Surface-Confined Hydroxyl Radical Chemistry in Complex Wastewater
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Electro-oxidation technology holds great promise for wastewater treatment, yet its practical application remains hindered by insufficient selectivity in oxidative species generation and limited electrode stability under harsh operating conditions. Here, we devise a layer-by-layer anion–cation engineering strategy to fabricate an Sb–F-stitched SnO2 bilayer anode (SF–SnO2 BA), in which a fluorine-regulated SnO2 catalytic layer is interfacially anchored onto a dense Sb–SnO2 interlayer coated on a Ti foam scaffold. This hierarchically stitched architecture simultaneously modulates interfacial charge transport and stabilizes the catalytic layer, leading to markedly enhanced electrocatalytic oxidation performance across a broad pH range (1–11). When integrated into a scalable flow-through electro-oxidation system, SF–SnO2 BA enabled highly efficient mineralization (>80%) of four representative industrial wastewaters at low energy consumption. Furthermore, the system also demonstrated remarkable operational durability, sustaining high mineralization efficiency (60–80%) over 14 consecutive days during continuous treatment of real aniline wastewater from a coal chemical plant. In situ spectroscopic investigations coupled with theoretical calculations collectively elucidated that water molecules are initially oxidized on the SF–SnO2 BA surface to form Sn–OH intermediates, which are subsequently transformed into Sn–O species at elevated potentials. Notably, the cooperative F···Sn–O* structural motif directs the generation of surface-confined •OH, which acts as the dominant oxidative species for pollutant degradation. This interfacially stitched bilayer anode offers a viable route toward green and sustainable electrochemical oxidation technologies for practical wastewater treatment.

papers.title: Lipophilic Redox Mediators Reprogram Intracellular Electron Flow to Promote Arsenic Methylation in Soil Fermentative Bacteria
papers.abstract: Anaerobic arsenic (As) methylation by fermentative microorganisms, particularly Clostridium-related populations, controls As speciation, mobility, and volatilization in flooded paddy soils, yet the mechanisms promoting this process remain poorly understood. Here, we reveal that phenazine- and phenoxazine-like redox mediators can enhance anaerobic As methylation via reshaping the intracellular electron allocation in a representative As-methylating fermentative bacterium. We integrated As speciation analysis, metabolite profiling, proteomics, and metabolic-flux modeling to determine how resazurin, as a represenative lipophilic redox mediator, reshapes fermentative metabolism and methylated As (MeAs) formation. The membrane-permeable redox mediator resazurin increased the apparent rate constant of MeAs formation by up to fourfold relative to the hydrophilic mediator anthraquinone-2,6-disulfonic acid (AQDS). Unlike AQDS, resazurin enhanced dimethylarsine formation while establishing a more reducing intracellular environment by diverting electrons from hydrogen evolution, indicating altered intracellular electron disposal. At the proteomic level, resazurin induced coordinated increases in As(III) methyltransferase (ArsM) and proteins involved in S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) biosynthesis, representing the primary molecular responses associated with enhanced As methylation. Proteins involved in amino-acid-fueled energy conservation and redox homeostasis were also enriched, potentially creating favorable cellular conditions for SAM-dependent As methylation. In a paddy-soil-derived fermentative consortium, resazurin likewise enhanced MeAs production and increased transcript levels of Clostridium-associated arsM and the SAM synthetase gene (metK). These findings identify lipophilicity-dependent, redox-compound-mediated intracellular electron flow reprogramming as a previously underappreciated control on anaerobic As methylation and provide a mechanistic basis for predicting MeAs formation in flooded soil environments.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights into alkaline hydrogen evolution over CoP/iron-phosphide heterojunctions

Hydrogen-Ion-Mediated Ni/Ni(OH)2 Dual Sites to Synergistically Accelerate *OH/Organics Adsorption for Highly Efficient Electrochemical 5-Amino-1 H -tetrazole Electrooxidation within a Wide Potential Range
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-rich azo-tetrazole compounds are essential structural scaffolds for energetic materials, dyes, and agrochemicals, owing to their favorable energetic and physicochemical properties. Potassium 5,5′-azotetrazolate (PZT), as a representative and efficient nitrogen-rich azo-tetrazole material, is conventionally synthesized via thermochemical oxidative coupling, which suffers from safety hazards and environmental pollution. Electrochemical synthesis offers a compelling alternative, but the severe competitive oxygen evolution reaction (OER) impedes achieving highly-efficient N–N coupling activity and Faradaic efficiency (FE). Herein, a core–shell CF@CuO@Ni/Ni(OH)2 electrode is fabricated through controlled H+-mediated electrodeposition. The CF@CuO core provides a three-dimensional (3D) conductive scaffold and suppresses the competing OER, while the Ni0/Ni(OH)2 shell undergoes electrochemical reconstruction into coexisting NiO/NiOOH working phases. The catalyst reaches 10 mA·cm–2 at 1.16 V vs RHE and maintains a Faradaic efficiency above 94% over a broad potential range of 1.2–1.6 V. Combined electrochemical, spectroscopic, kinetic, and computational analyses prove that surface-adsorbed *OH initiates 5-AT dehydrogenative coupling via a PCET pathway on the reconstructed NiO/NiOOH surface. NiO triggers synergistic *OH/5-AT adsorption, while NiOOH facilitates dehydrogenation. In a continuous-flow AEM electrolyzer, the system operates at 500 mA cm–2 over 300 h while sustaining PZT production (purity ≥99%) and H2 evolution. Extension to DAT and DAF further demonstrates the transferability of the catalyst toward related amino-functionalized N-heterocycles undergoing oxidative N–N coupling. This work establishes that reconstructed NiO/NiOOH dual sites, supported on an OER-suppressing CuO scaffold, enable selective and energy-efficient N–N oxidative coupling of amino heterocycles.

papers.title: Electrolyte Cation Engineering Selectively Regulates Competing Urea Oxidation Pathways
papers.abstract: The electrochemical urea oxidation reaction (UOR) has emerged as an attractive anodic reaction for various energy conversion systems. Recently, increasing attention has been directed toward controlling UOR selectivity on Ni-based electrocatalysts following the recognition that the UOR can produce over-oxidized products. However, existing studies have focused predominantly on catalyst design to regulate surface-bound intermediates, whereas whether electrolyte-mediated noncovalent interactions can selectively control competing UOR pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we show that rational electrolyte engineering using alkali-metal cations selectively regulates the UOR pathway by modulating the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network. Electrochemical rate deconvolution and product analysis reveal that weakly hydrated cations selectively accelerate the direct oxidation pathway, promoting the formation of the over-oxidized NO2– and NCO– products, while leaving the indirect pathway essentially unaffected. In situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) measurements, together with molecular dynamics simulations of cation hydration dynamics, indicate that weakly hydrated cations create a more dynamic interfacial water environment with faster water exchange, thereby facilitating interfacial OH–-mediated successive dehydrogenation during direct urea oxidation. Leveraging this mechanistic understanding, the electrolyte-engineering strategy was applied to a cascade urea-to-ammonia conversion system, achieving a urea-to-ammonia conversion efficiency of 77.5% and approximately threefold higher ammonia productivity in CsOH than in LiOH. These findings establish electrolyte engineering as a complementary strategy to catalyst design and highlight noncovalent electrolyte–electrode interactions as an effective handle for controlling reaction pathways and product selectivity in an integrated UOR-based nitrogen conversion system.

papers.title: Deciphering the Role of Au in CO Reduction on Cu: From Atomic Sites to a Stabilized Proton-Transfer Interface
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Incorporating gold (Au) into copper (Cu)-based electrocatalysts effectively enhances the conversion of CO into multicarbon products, yet the fundamental role of Au remains elusive due to limited mechanistic insight. Using a Au-doped basic copper chloride as a platform precatalyst, we demonstrate that the in situ formation of stable Cu3Au intermetallics during operation substantially alters the CO electroreduction pathway. Using multispectroscopic analyses combined with theoretical calculations, we find that the in situ-formed Cu3Au structure likely plays a synergistic role by (i) optimizing *CO adsorption and surface coverage to promote C–C coupling and (ii) restructuring the interfacial water network to strengthen hydrogen bonding, thereby shifting the dominant proton-transfer pathway from a Langmuir–Hinshelwood mechanism to an Eley–Rideal mechanism. This reconfiguration suppresses the hydrogen evolution reaction and adsorbed hydrogen-mediated pathways while promoting direct proton donation from interfacial water for the formation of acetate. Consequently, the optimized catalyst achieves an acetate Faradaic efficiency of 80.3% at −1.05 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode with a partial current density of −492.7 mA cm–2. These findings underscore how adaptive electrochemical reconstruction can design active sites and modulate interfacial proton-transfer dynamics to steer CO valorization toward targeted products.

papers.title: Rigor and Reproducibility in Electrocatalysis: Integrating Theory and Experiment
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Electrocatalysis is central to electrified energy conversion technologies, including the production of fuels and chemicals from renewable electricity. In recent years, atomistic modeling based on density functional theory (DFT) has become an indispensable tool for catalysis researchers because it can provide a molecular-level perspective of catalytic reactivity that is otherwise inaccessible through experimental measurements. Computational electrocatalysis model inputs are intended to capture fundamental understanding of the complex interfacial environment of the catalytic active site, but they rely on practical approximations that can affect the reliability of insights gained from DFT. This Perspective outlines a framework for rigorous and reproducible integration of theory and experiment in heterogeneous electrocatalysis research. We discuss state-of-the-art computational methods and sources of error in model development and interpretation. We describe opportunities for validation of theoretical models and experimental interpretations as they pertain to the structure of active sites, reaction energetics, and microkinetic modeling. We provide examples to help computational researchers develop models that move beyond obtaining qualitative agreement with reactivity trends, and toward the development of rigorous mechanistic insights that can be leveraged to predict promising new catalysts or operating conditions. Rigor and reproducibility are enhanced when theory and experiment have multiple nodes of connection, thereby enhancing the longevity and robustness of conclusions and insights about electrocatalytic reactivity.

papers.title: Selective Electrochemical E –Semihydrogenation of Alkyl Alkynes with Main Metal Electrodes and Water
papers.abstract: The semihydrogenation reaction of alkynes to E-alkenes is still a challenge in modern and sustainable organic chemistry, particularly for alkyl alkynes where allyl H-abstraction, alkynyl hydrofunctionalization, and overhydrogenation by reactions easily occur. Here we show that a selective E–electrosemihydrogenation reaction of alkyl alkynes proceeds with Mg and Al as sacrificial electrodes in THF/water mixtures. The reaction is extendable to aromatic alkynes and deuteration processes, proceeds with >98% Faradaic efficiency (FA) in an undivided cell, avoids the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), and achieves E/Z ratios >3:1, three times higher than any recent electro(catalytic) method reported as far as we know. Mechanistic studies based on reactive, kinetic, isotopic, and computational experiments, among others, reveal that the success of this transition-metal-free electrochemical semihydrogenation reaction relies on the direct one-electron cathodic reduction of the alkyne, circumventing the typical H activation triggered by transition metals and enabling the rapid isomerization of the so-formed vinyl anion radical to the more stable E isomer after final protonation. These results open the way to directly obtain E-alkyl alkenes from the corresponding alkynes with just highly abundant metals, water, and electricity, with broad application in industrial chemistry, herein demonstrated for the gram-scale synthesis of a pheromone precursor.

papers.title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Chiral 1,4‐Dicarbonyls Bearing All‐Carbon Quaternary Stereocenters via Photoredox/Nickel Dual Catalyzed Tandem Radical Addition/Oxidation
papers.abstract: The asymmetric synthesis of 1,4‐dicarbonyl compounds bearing all‐carbon quaternary stereocenters remains a significant challenge in organic synthesis. Herein, we report a photoredox/nickel dual‐catalyzed tandem radical addition and oxidation protocol that directly converts β ‐keto esters and styrenes into enantioenriched 1,4‐dicarbonyl products in a single operation. This approach harnesses the synergistic cooperation of a photocatalyst and a chiral nickel catalyst to generate α ‐carbonyl radicals chelated to the chiral catalyst, via single‐electron oxidation of in situ‐formed Ni‐enolate complexes. The resulting radical intermediates are stereoselectively trapped by alkenes, and the ensuing benzyl radicals are subsequently oxidized by molecular oxygen to furnish the desired scaffolds. This catalytic system operates under mild conditions using molecular oxygen as the terminal oxidant, thereby obviating the need for prefunctionalized coupling partners while offering excellent functional group compatibility and broad substrate scope.

papers.title: Light‐Driven Surface Lattice Oxygen Activation in Oxygen Evolution
papers.abstract: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a key bottleneck in sustainable hydrogen production and energy conversion. Conventional pathways such as the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) and lattice oxygen oxidation mechanism (LOM) both suffer from electron‐transfer inefficiencies at their potential‐determining steps ( * OOH formation in AEM and deprotonation in LOM) and structural instability (metal oxidation in AEM and oxygen‐vacancy accumulation in LOM). As a result, a unified mechanism that simultaneously overcomes these kinetic limitations and structural degradation processes remains absent. Here, we present a light‐driven surface lattice oxygen activation mechanism (LSOM) that synergizes photoexcitation and electrocatalysis to activate surface lattice oxygen into high‐energy non‐bonding orbitals, enabling their direct participation in O─O bond formation. This strategy circumvents the potential‐determining steps inherent to both AEM and LOM, while preserving metal oxidation states and lattice structural integrity. Experimental validation confirms remarkable enhancements in electrocatalytic activity and stability, outperforming conventional OER systems. By unifying catalytic efficiency with structural durability, the LSOM redefines the design principles for OER and establishes a universal framework for robust energy conversion technologies.

papers.title: Descriptor‐Guided Stabilization of Reconstructed Active Phases for High‐Activity and Durable CO 2 ‐to‐Formate Conversion
papers.abstract: Sn oxides are promising CO 2 RR electrocatalysts for formate production, but their high activity is difficult to sustain because cathodic reconstruction can over‐reduce active oxide‐derived surfaces to metallic Sn. This dynamic evolution makes it challenging to identify and stabilize the true working‐state active phase. Here, we construct a descriptor‐guided framework that links dynamic Sn‐oxide reconstruction with electronic‐structure evolution and formate‐producing activity to identify and stabilize the favorable working‐state active phase. Electronic‐structure analysis shows that the optimal Sn x O y /Sn surface stabilizes the *OCHO intermediate through coupled charge‐polarization redistribution and Sn 5 s /5 p orbital modulation. To quantify this effect, we develop a TD descriptor integrating Bader charge, Sn 5 p coupling, and Sn 5 s lone‐pair activation, which exhibits a volcano‐type correlation with the limiting free energy, with the minimum at TD = 0.67 corresponding to the most favorable reconstructed Sn x O y /Sn surface. Guided by this descriptor, amorphous SnO 2 is designed to stabilize the favorable Sn x O y /Sn working state and suppress deep reduction, achieving an HCOO − partial current density of 438.0 mA cm −2 at −1.8 V vs. RHE, 1.8 times that of commercial SnO 2 . This work provides a descriptor‐guided strategy for stabilizing reconstructed active phases in CO 2 RR.

papers.title: Dynamic Hydrogen‑Bond Network Accelerates Lattice Oxygen Regeneration for High‑Current‑Density Seawater Electrolysis
papers.abstract: Seawater electrolysis for green H 2 production is hindered by the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and chloride corrosion at the anode. Although the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) can effectively reduce the overpotential, the sluggish mass transport of OH − at high current densities disrupts the oxygen release–regeneration balance, ultimately leading to a trade‐off between activity and stability. Here, we demonstrate that yttrium (Y) and carboxylate co‐doping reconstruct the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network of NiFe oxyhydroxide, dynamically accelerating OH − delivery and enabling rapid regeneration of lattice oxygen. This catalyst maintains a high LOM contribution (51.7%–54%) while achieving exceptional durability and Cl − resistance. In situ Raman, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), and rotating ring‐disk electrode (RRDE) analyses confirm rapid peroxide intermediate formation, lattice oxygen participation, and negligible chlorine evolution. The anion‐exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer delivers 1000 mA cm −2 at 1.79 V and operates stably for 800 h in alkaline seawater. This work establishes interfacial hydrogen‐bonding engineering as a generalizable strategy to break the activity–stability trade‐off for robust seawater electrolysis.

Synergistic-Tandem Active Sites Engineered in Pd-Doped Mo5N6 Nanosheets for Efficient CO2 Photoreduction to Acetic Acid
papers.abstract: CO2 photoreduction into multicarbon products such as acetic acid represents a promising strategy for addressing the greenhouse effect and energy shortages. However, the process is limited by kinetically sluggish C–C coupling and inefficient proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET). Herein, we construct Nv-Pdδ+ tandem active sites in Mo5N6 nanosheets via low-valent Pdδ+ (2 < δ < 4) doping, which simultaneously introduces abundant stable nitrogen vacancies (Nv) and adjacent Pdδ+ centers. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the Nv sites promote CO2 activation and reduce the energy barrier for *CO dimerization, while the neighboring Pdδ+ sites efficiently drive water splitting to supply H*, thereby facilitating the hydrogenation of key *OCCO intermediates. Accordingly, the optimized Pd0.5-Mo5N6 achieves a high acetic acid selectivity of 90.1% with an evolution rate of 33.24 μmol·g–1·h–1 under solar irradiation. This work establishes a tandem active-site design strategy for efficient and durable photocatalytic synthesis of multicarbon products from CO2.

papers.title: Catalytic Asymmetric Diels–Alder Reaction of β,β-Disubstituted Enals with Cyclopentadiene: Syntheses of (−)-Camphene, (−)-β-Santalene, and (−)-( Z )-β-Santalol
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Despite the long and rich history of the Diels–Alder reaction, certain aspects of its scope still remain remarkably underexplored. Most prominently, reactions with β,β-disubstituted enals as dienophiles are scarcely represented in the literature. The first general and highly enantioselective method, enabled by a strongly acidic and confined imidodiphosphorimidate organocatalyst, is reported here. The reaction tolerates a broad range of enals, including substrates with functional groups and complex alkenyl substituents, delivering the corresponding cycloadducts in good yields and excellent enantioselectivity. The synthetic utility of the method is further highlighted by concise asymmetric total syntheses of (−)-camphene, (−)-β-santalene, and (−)-(Z)-β-santalol from inexpensive starting materials.

papers.title: Electroenzymatic Cascade Enables Amino Acid Synthesis through Simultaneous Nitrite Reduction and NADH Regeneration
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Amino acids are central to life and the chemical industry, yet their sustainable synthesis remains a challenge. An electroenzymatic cascade offers a promising alternative by combining the electron/proton transfer capability of electrocatalysis with the exceptional specificity of biocatalysis. Here we present a conceptually distinct electroenzymatic cascade platform that integrates electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction, NADH regeneration, and enzymatic reductive amination. Using l-glutamate (l-Glu) as a model, we demonstrate that with Cu nanowires as the bifunctional electrocatalyst, the system generates NH4+ and biologically active NADH in situ, driving the production of l-Glu under mild conditions. The coupled cascade not only shifts the reaction equilibrium forward but also provides a favorable orientation and a proton-rich environment for the bioactive cofactor, boosting overall selectivity of bioactive NADH. The modular design allows straightforward adaptation to diverse substrates and electrodes, demonstrating the broad generality of this platform. This work establishes a sustainable and versatile strategy for amino acid synthesis and opens new directions for electroenzymatic production of nitrogen-containing chemicals.

papers.title: Decoupling OH and H Binding via Dual‐Site Conductive MOFs for Efficient Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: Efficient regulation of the hydrogen and hydroxyl binding energies (HBE/OHBE) lies at the core of developing high‐performance alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts, yet it remains challenging due to the inherent correlation between the two binding energies. Herein, we demonstrate a d ‐electron modulation strategy on dual‐metal sites to break the scaling constraint and synergistically optimize HBE and OHBE. A well‐defined Cu‐based two‐dimensional conductive metal–organic framework (Cu‐HHTP) serves as a universal host to incorporate various 3 d transition metals (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu), yielding M–Cu dual sites with finely tunable d ‐electron configurations. Density functional theory calculations combined with experiments reveal that higher d ‐electron occupancy of the secondary metal site lowers the d ‐band center, and the water dissociation energy barrier exhibits a typical volcano‐type trend. The Co–Cu dual sites at the volcano apex promote the Volmer step through optimized OHBE and water adsorption. Meanwhile, this dual‐site configuration promotes the rearrangement of interfacial water molecules by disrupting the hydrogen‐bond network, thereby optimizing HBE. This work decouples HBE and OHBE via d ‐electron configuration, shifting the design paradigm from empirical screening to predictive design.

papers.title: Rh 0 –Rh δ+ Synergy Enables Hydroxyl‐Directed Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation of Guaiacol
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic hydrogenation (ECH) of lignin‐derived guaiacol offers an appealing route toward sustainable chemical production but is impeded by the exceptional stability of aromatic rings. Conventional rhodium catalysts with electronically symmetric Rh 0 –Rh 0 sites generally activate guaiacol through Rh 0 ‐arene π interactions. However, the induced electronic perturbation remains largely delocalized over the arene π system, resulting in only limited local polarization and sluggish dearomatizing hydrogenation kinetics. Here, we introduce a hydroxyl‐directed activation strategy that exploits the phenolic hydroxyl group as an intrinsic handle for aromatic‐ring activation. Spatially adjacent Rh 0 and Rh δ+ sites (Rh 0 –Rh δ+ ) were constructed in RhO x clusters through lattice‐oxygen‐mediated electrochemical reconstruction. The electron‐deficient Rh δ+ sites selectively anchor the phenolic hydroxyl group, perturbing resonance donation from the phenolic oxygen into the aromatic ring and inducing asymmetric redistribution of aromatic π‐electron density. This hydroxyl‐directed adsorption simultaneously orients the aromatic ring toward neighboring Rh 0 sites, thereby promoting d→π* back‐donation and lowering the hydrogenation barrier. The resultant Rh 0 –Rh δ+ catalyst achieves a 2‐methoxycyclohexanol production rate of 197.51 mmol h −1 g Rh −1 , which is 22‐fold higher than that of Rh 0 –Rh 0 . Our findings establish hydroxyl‐directed aromatic‐ring activation as an effective strategy for overcoming aromatic inertia, providing a design principle for the electrocatalytic upgrading of lignin‐derived aromatics.

papers.title: Redox‑Gated Molecular Switching of CO 2 Self‑Poisoning on Quinone Electrocatalysts Enables In Situ Self‑Regeneration
papers.abstract: Quinone‐based metal‐free electrocatalysts offer a sustainable route for oxygen activation and water purification, yet their persistent activity decay has remained poorly understood. Here, we identify mineralization‐derived CO 2 as the major cause of a previously overlooked self‐poisoning pathway in quinone‑based electrocatalysts: CO 2 accumulates at the electrode–electrolyte interface and forms stable carbonate adducts with reduced quinone moieties, blocking the active sites for two‐electron oxygen reduction to H 2 O 2 and consequently suppressing ·OH generation through the cascade oxygen‐reduction pathway. Electrochemical analysis further reveals that CO 2 adduction reorganizes the native quinone redox transitions into potential‐dependent carbonate‐bound states, allowing the occupied quinone centers to be reversibly regenerated by oxidative pulses. Leveraging this principle, we developed a pulsed electrocatalytic strategy that periodically reoxidizes the quinone catalyst in situ, dynamically reversing CO 2 poisoning without requiring chemical regenerants or thermal treatment. Across structurally diverse pollutants at neutral pH, this strategy accelerates degradation kinetics by up to 725.3% and retains up to 93.6% of its 2 h diclofenac removal efficiency after 12 h of continuous operation. More broadly, the redox‐gated CO 2 switching mechanism provides a generalizable design paradigm for mitigating CO 2 ‐induced deactivation in electrocatalytic systems prone to local CO 2 buildup, including CO 2 electrolysis, electrosynthetic biomass conversion, and electrochemical nitrogen fixation.

papers.title: Reversible Breathing of Cu─Co Dual‐Atom Sites Enables Spatially Proximal C─N Coupling for Urea Electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic urea synthesis via the Langmuir–Hinshelwood pathway demands spatially proximal active sites to synchronize the generation and cross‐coupling of C‐ and N‐derived intermediates. Heteronuclear dual‐atom catalysts offer chemically differentiated sites for this purpose, yet whether their bimetallic centers remain static or dynamically evolve during C─N coupling remains unresolved. Here, we construct a well‐defined N 3 ─Cu─Co─N 3 dual‐atom site for the electrochemical coreduction of CO 2 and NO 3 − to synthesize urea and uncover its reversible, electric‐field‐driven structural breathing under electrocatalytic conditions, affording a maximum urea yield rate of 4828.4 ± 136.5 µg h −1 mg cat −1 and a Faradaic efficiency of 56.8 ± 7.6% at −1.2 V (vs. RHE). Operando x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) revealed a reversible, electric‐field‐driven breathing‐like modulation of the Cu─Co distance, characterized by Cu─Co contraction and Cu─N/Co─N elongation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that the Cu─Co distance reaches a minimum of 2.16 Å in the *CONH 2 ‐bound configuration formed during the initial C─N coupling step. The adaptive contraction brings C‐ and N‐intermediates into close proximity to enable C─N coupling, thereby reconfiguring heteronuclear dual‐atom sites from static pairs into dynamically responsive centers and highlighting field‐tunable metal–metal distance as a catalytic design lever.

papers.title: Tailoring the p-band center of biomass-derived carbon for high-efficiency electrocatalytic H2O2 production
Kinetic Limitations of Single-Atom Catalysts in Hydrazine Oxidation
papers.abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) have attracted considerable interest, displaying impressive performance for a wide plethora of electrocatalytic reactions. However, the important question whether isolated sites are always beneficial remains unresolved. Here, by using the hydrazine oxidation reaction (HzOR) as a model reaction, we examine how isolated single-atom metal sites restrict the adsorption mode of intermediates to the monodentate configuration, which leads to weak intermediate stabilization and poor reaction kinetics. This contrasts with bulk metal sites where availability of the bidentate adsorption configuration offers better intermediate stabilization and dehydrogenation kinetics. As a result, Ir, Pt, and Pd SACs were found to require high HzOR overpotentials of 0.90, 1.21, and 1.19 V at 3 mA cm–2, respectively. Comparatively, their Ir, Pt, Pd nanoparticle counterparts with similar metal loading exhibit considerably lower overpotentials of only 0.35, 0.83, and 0.64 V at 3 mA cm–2, respectively. Taken together, our work contributes towards a more complete understanding of SACs, emphasizing the importance of considering site structure and the mechanistic demands of the reaction.

papers.title: Trash to Treasure: PFAS‐Functionalized MOFs for Boosted Piezocatalytic H 2 Production
papers.abstract: Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) hold broad prospects in piezocatalysis because of their high surface area, porosity, and tunable structures, yet pristine MOFs frequently suffer from poor piezocatalytic response. Herein, this study pioneers a novel strategy using pollutant perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA) as a functional additive to post‐synthetically modify MOF‐808(Hf), fabricating MOF‐808(Hf)‐F for piezocatalytic hydrogen production. PFHxA modification remarkably enhances the polarity of MOF‐808(Hf) (dipole moment from 8.90 to 12.58 D) and piezoelectricity (d 33 from 63.70 to 234.30 pm V −1 ), boosting electron‐hole separation verified by electrochemical and in situ photoluminescence characterizations. Consequently, MOF‐808(Hf)‐F achieves an excellent piezocatalytic H 2 evolution rate of 2811.4 µmol g −1 h −1 , 10.5‐fold higher than the pristine counterpart and superior to that of numerous reported MOF‐based piezocatalysts. In addition, MOF‐808(Hf) achieves a PFHxA removal efficiency of approximately 40.1% from water. This work realizes simultaneous per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) removal and efficient energy production, with excellent universality for Hf‐based MOFs with unsaturated metal sites.
